rows.response_text: The marginal cost (MC) curve initially declines and then increases at a certain point. It intersects the average total cost and average variable cost curves at their minimum points. This U-shaped structure of the MC curve is due to the increase and then decrease of marginal returns, reflecting the law of diminishing marginal returns. The lowest point of the average variable cost is called the shutdown point in a competitive model, as firms will not produce in the short run if the price is below this cost.
